title: New-Patient Fee Ratio for Routine Eye Exams on Vision Plans
content:
**Desk reference — Vision Plans exam visits**

A **new-patient fee ratio** applies to the scheduled exam fee of a routine eye exam at a participating location, by these terms.

**The look-back.** The record looked at is the latest routine eye exam of the patient under the same provider agreement as the visit whose remark is paid or out-of-network reimbursement paid.
- When that latest exam is the only such exam on its date and has been reversed, there is taken to be none, and no earlier exam is looked at.
- When there are several such exams on that date, a reversal of one leaves that date standing.

**When the ratio applies.** The ratio applies unless that latest exam is dated on or before the visit and less than thirty-six whole calendar months (36) before it. A month is complete on the same day number.

| Look-back result | Channel of the visit | New-patient fee ratio |
|---|---|---|
| No such exam, or one dated after the visit, or one 36 whole months or more before it | Participating independent practice | 1.30 |
| Same | Participating retail-chain location | 1.25 |
| An exam on or before the visit and less than 36 whole months before it (an established patient) | Any participating location | 1 |
| Any | Out of network | 1 |

**Boundary (hypothetical dates).** With the latest paid exam under the same agreement on 20 June, a visit on 19 June three years later is 35 whole months later: the patient is established and the ratio is 1. A visit on 20 June three years later is 36 whole months later: the ratio of 1.30 (independent practice) or 1.25 (retail chain) applies.

**Points of judgement**
- *An exam at another practice:* an exam under a different provider agreement does not make the patient established at this one.
- *A reversed exam:* a lone reversed exam on the latest date counts as none, and earlier exams are not then consulted.
